objective.statement: Read and place notes in the bass clef, and say why it is called the F clef.
successCriteria: I can recognise the bass clef and know it marks F on the 4th line.
I can name the bass-clef line notes G B D F A and space notes A C E G.
I can write a note in the bass clef.

explanation.text: The bass clef is used for lower notes. It looks like a hook with two dots. The dots sit either side of the 4th line, and that line is F, which is why the bass clef is also called the F clef.

music.textAlternative: A bass-clef stave with one note on the 4th line, labelled F, between the two dots of the clef.

explanation.caption: The 4th line from the bottom is F. The clef's two dots sit either side of it.

music.textAlternative: A bass-clef stave with five notes on the lines, labelled G, B, D, F and A from the bottom.

explanation.caption: Bass-clef line notes from the bottom: G B D F A.

music.textAlternative: A bass-clef stave with four notes in the spaces, labelled A, C, E and G from the bottom.

explanation.caption: Bass-clef space notes from the bottom: A C E G.

explanation.text: The lines and spaces are the same, but the names are different. The bottom line is E in the treble clef and G in the bass clef, so always check the clef first.
Make up your own sentences for G B D F A and A C E G. The sillier they are, the easier they are to remember.

music.textAlternative: Three bass-clef notes: F on the 4th line, G on the bottom line and A on the top line, each linked to a key.

steps: Tap F, on the 4th line between the clef's two dots. This is the reference note for the bass clef.
Tap G on the bottom line, then A on the top line. Their keys light up on the keyboard.
Compare with the treble clef: the same bottom line has a different name here.
demonstration.textAlternative: Three bass-clef notes, F on the 4th line, G on the bottom line and A on the top line, each tied to its keyboard key. Sound is optional.

guided.prompt: The two dots of the bass clef sit either side of this line. What is the note?

music.textAlternative: A bass-clef stave with one semibreve on the 4th line.

hints: Find the clef's reference note first (G on line 2 in treble, F on line 4 in bass).
Count lines and spaces from the bottom.
The note is on the 4th line. The bottom line of the bass clef is G: count up (or down) one letter for each line and space.

feedback.correct: Yes: F. The bass clef marks F on the 4th line.

mistakes.line-space-swap: Look closely: is the line running through the note-head, or is the note sitting between two lines?
mistakes.clef-confusion: That would be right in another clef. Check the clef at the start of the stave first.
mistakes.counted-from-top: Lines and spaces are counted from the bottom of the stave upwards.
mistakes.off-by-step: You're one step away. Find a note you know for certain and count up or down from it.
mistakes.ledger-miscount: Count the ledger lines one at a time, from the stave outwards.
mistakes.accidental-ignored: The letter is right, but check for a sharp, flat or natural — in the key signature or in front of the note.

feedback.fallback: Not quite. Start from the clef and count from a note you know.
